By Amanda Cantrell and Laura BenitezOctober 29, 2026 at 7:38 PM UTCBookmark

Ares Management Corp. is avoiding financing deals to back the high-powered processing units that run sophisticated AI models, opting to invest in the data centers that house them instead.
The asset manager has concerns that if it backs graphics processing units, it could get stuck holding assets that may be obsolete not long after they’re released, said a person close to the firm, who asked not to be identified because the information is private.

item.title: Lenders Seek to Sell Debt of Rovensa as Firm Burns Cash
item.description: Lenders to Partners Group-backed Rovensa are looking to offload the debt of the Iberian agricultural products maker as the firm burns through cash.

item.title: Investors Buy Rogers (RCI), BCE, Telus Stocks After Canada Telecom Selloff
item.description: Investors are bargain hunting in Canadian telecommunication stocks after rising government-bond yields and competition from SpaceX sparked steep declines in the group.

item.title: Tech Stocks Slide as Alphabet’s Record Plunge Revives AI Fears
item.description: Tech stocks were dragged lower by a record drop in Alphabet Inc. after disappointing results renewed investor concerns about the threat that artificial intelligence poses to its core business.

item.title: Agnico Eagle (AEM) Flags Diesel Risk to Gold Output Costs Next Year
item.description: Agnico Eagle Mines Ltd. warned that rising diesel prices risk raising the cost of producing gold by as much as $80 per ounce next year, signaling mounting inflationary pressures for the mining industry.

item.title: Amazon’s Ailing Stock Needs Booming Cloud Growth to Revive Rally
item.description: Blistering cloud growth sent Amazon.com Inc. shares soaring after its last earnings report. Now with more than half those gains gone, the firm needs to deliver a repeat performance in order to reignite its faltering stock.
